intro: You heard it too, didn't you? The bell beneath the woods. It has not rung since my grandmother was a girl.
And now the goblins are gathering around the shrine.
The roots have gone dark. Even your wolf can smell it. Bring me three Moonleaf sprigs; their light will open the old sanctuary.
We'll find what woke beneath Willowbrook.
Follow the northern trail, cross Sunstream, and look for the purple flowers. Come back before entering the ruin.
herbs: All three! Hold still. A little moonlight, a little courage... there.
Take these potions. Follow Whisperwood north, cross Sunstream into Sunmeadow Plains, then reach the shrine at the far end of the road. Below are two seals, guarded by creatures and puzzles.
Break the seals, then find the source?
Yes. But the guardian was once our protector. If it draws back its branches, raise your guard. Do not meet that blow head-on.
reminder: Three purple Moonleaf plants: two in Whisperwood, one on the plains beyond Sunstream. They are marked purple on your map. Your wolf will keep you company.
ready: The Moonleaf charm will open the shrine across Sunstream. Find both root seals below, then wake the guardian from its nightmare.
shrine: These carvings... a guardian sheltering the village beneath its branches.
Remember what we protect. That is the oath, not the sword.
Then let's bring our guardian home.
sealed: The stone door is alive with black roots. Mira may know how to loosen them. We should finish gathering Moonleaf first.
dungeon: The air is colder here. Two chambers, two seals. Stone dials to the west and old bells to the east. Their inscriptions must tell us how to wake them.
The wolf's ears prick toward the darkness. Somewhere below, wood creaks like a ship at sea.
seal: The roots loosen. A little light is finding its way back.
Your companion nudges your hand, then watches the northern passage.
boss_locked: Two root seals bind the guardian. We need to cleanse both side chambers before the heart will open.
boss: SMALL... FLAMES... WHY DO YOU BURN MY ROOTS?
We came to help. Willowbrook still remembers you.
THE BELL... THE DARK BENEATH... I CANNOT...
Then let us carry the light until you can.
boss_win: The bell... is quiet. Little oathkeeper, I had forgotten the sound of birds.
They'll be waiting when you wake.
Take this living ember. Let Willowbrook know: the roots remember.
ending: The stream is clear again. I knew before I saw you.
The guardian was trapped. Something deeper was pulling at its roots.
Then there will be another road, another day. For now, you brought our forest back.
I'd say it has only just begun.
epilogue: Listen. Birds, the stream, your wolf pretending not to want another treat. I could get used to this kind of quiet.
So could I. For a little while.
marsh_royal: Mira sent word of the restored guardian. His Majesty came to Reedcross when the waterworks failed. He asked to hear from you personally.
You helped Willowbrook without a crown to command you. That is the sort of service this realm needs.
I have opened the royal granary to Reedcross. But grain cannot mend its failing sluices. Speak to Warden Iona; listen before you draw your weapon.
The forest guardian was wounded by a broken oath. Could these waters share its roots?
Then help me keep an older promise: no village abandoned to the flood. Take this travel purse. I will remain until the evacuation boats are ready.
marsh_iona: The ancient waterworks are drowning our fields. Blue lanterns burn where no ferryman walks, and the keeper no longer hears us.
Bring a water-reading from each of the three blue survey stones along the causeway. They will tell us whether the seal is broken or merely blocked.
marsh_key: All three readings point inward. The keeper is trapping the flood to protect a covenant nobody remembers.
Take this sluice key. In the reliquary: drain the west basin, cross its bed, then divert the east channel. Do not mistake an open valve for a safe crossing.
The inscription says: EMPTY the bowl; TURN the river; QUIET the heart. Listen when the keeper gathers a tide.
marsh_after: The channels are running clear. You did not destroy our keeper; you freed it from an oath twisted against the people it protected.
My soldiers will repair the causeway. You have my thanks—and payment, not merely praise.
The tablet names an Emberglass archive in the Sahir desert. Someone removed a passage about the first closing of the gates.
Seek answers when the southern road is ready. Until then, rest here. Reedcross owes you safe harbour.
marsh_complete: The reliquary is quiet. The Emberglass tablet remains your next lead; the Sahir route is not yet open.
marsh_reeds: My patients cannot wait for the flood to fall. I need four silverreed bundles from the marked banks along the causeway. Watch for leeches by the water.
marsh_patrol: Reed Stalkers have taken the causeway. Defeat three and I can bring the medicine boat through. You can clear them before or after speaking to me.
